sections.title: Rig & Vessel Day-Rates
sections.description: Benchmark day-rate trends for jackups, floaters and offshore support vessels across key regions.

items.title: Westwood: offshore rig dayrates mostly continue to fall in 2026
items.summary: Leading-edge jackup dayrates averaged just over $94,000/day year-to-date in 2026 (down 6% from 2025, ~24% below 2024's $123,000 average). Semisubmersibles averaged just under $340,000/day (Norway premium $436,000/day) and 6th/7th-gen drillships averaged ~$388,000/day. Global jackup utilisation fell 7 points year-on-year to 85%; floating rig utilisation slipped to 87%.
items.source_name: Riviera Maritime Media (citing Westwood Global Energy)

items.title: 2026 offshore challenge: softening demand puts brakes on day rates
items.summary: Near-term drillship day rates have fallen under $400,000/day amid expected 2026 oil oversupply exceeding 3 million boepd, though later contract work commands higher rates — over 40% of competitive 7th-gen drillships are already booked for 2027. Drillship utilisation is projected at 94% for 2026-2027, semisub utilisation rising to 88% in 2026, jackup utilisation holding at 91%+.

items.title: North Sea AHTS and PSV day rates hold firm on fleet attrition
items.summary: Large AHTS vessels in the North Sea are commanding $35,000-$55,000/day on short-term fixtures in 2026 (having briefly touched $60,000-$70,000/day in 2023-2024), while PSVs of 4,000+ DWT achieve $22,000-$32,000/day — levels not sustained since the 2013-2014 peak — driven by 300+ vessels scrapped or redeployed since 2015.

items.title: OSV rates and utilisation levels roar back in Southeast Asia
items.summary: Day rates for 'backbone' 5,150-bhp AHTS vessels reached $8,100/day and 8,000-bhp AHTS units recovered to $12,000/day, while larger 10,000-12,000-bhp AHTS units chartered at $16,000-$19,000/day and PSVs (1,000 m² clear deck) commanded $33,000-$36,000/day amid a regional shortage of 8,000-bhp AHTS tonnage.

items.title: GCC jackup dayrates keep sliding as Saudi Aramco suspensions linger
items.summary: Average GCC jackup dayrates fell from $108,484 in 2023 to $91,735 in 2024 and $89,865 in 2025, with 2026 forecast to remain in the low-to-high $80,000s/day; committed Middle East utilisation is projected to decline from 91% (2025) to 89% (2026) as, of 37 jackup contracts Saudi Aramco suspended, 22 rigs have since mobilised out of or committed to leave the Kingdom.

items.title: Valaris Q2 2026: drillship dayrate repricing lifts rates to $416k-$433k
items.summary: Valaris reported Q2 2026 operating revenue of $539.2m (down from $615.2m a year earlier) and net income of $50.4m. Contract repricing lifted drillship dayrates to $416,000-$433,000/day even as idle rigs and Middle East conflict costs (~$38m negative operating income impact YTD) weighed on results ahead of its pending all-stock merger with Transocean.

sections.title: Offshore Tenders & Contract Awards
sections.description: Recent EPC/EPCI awards, FIDs and charter contracts across oil & gas, offshore wind and defence.

items.title: Subsea7 wins pipeline installation contract for Who Dat East, US Gulf
items.summary: Subsea7 was awarded a sizeable contract (estimated $50-150 million) by LLOG Exploration, a Harbour Energy subsidiary, to install a 29-km steel catenary riser and pipe-in-pipe system plus umbilical and subsea controls for the Who Dat East development in ~1,300m water depth. Engineering starts immediately in Houston, offshore installation planned for 2028.

items.title: DOF secures transport and installation deal for North Sea floating wind
items.summary: DOF ASA was awarded a Transport & Installation contract for a floating offshore wind project in the North Sea, covering inshore marine operations, mooring system pre-lay, floating turbine tow-out and installation, and dynamic/static export cable installation. Contract value was not disclosed.

items.title: SLB OneSubsea awarded EPC contract for Eni's Baleine Phase 3, Ivory Coast
items.summary: SLB's OneSubsea joint venture was awarded a multi-well EPC contract by Eni for Phase 3 of the deepwater Baleine project offshore Cote d'Ivoire, covering subsea production systems for 13 wells including trees, umbilicals, manifolds, multiphase flowmeters, controls, installation and commissioning.

items.title: Saipem wins ~$2 billion EPCI contract for Kutei FPSO, Indonesia
items.summary: Saipem, via PT Saipem Indonesia in JV with PT Tripatra Engineers and Constructors, was awarded an EPCI contract worth ~$2 billion (Saipem's share) for a new FPSO for the Kutei Basin North Hub development offshore East Kalimantan, for client Eni North Ganal. Estimated project duration: 48 months.

items.title: US Navy awards $76.6bn for new Virginia- and Columbia-class submarines
items.summary: The US Navy awarded General Dynamics Electric Boat and Huntington Ingalls' Newport News Shipbuilding a combined $76.6 billion across two contracts: $42.1bn for nine Block VI Virginia-class attack submarines plus material for an additional unit, and $29.5bn for five Build II Columbia-class ballistic missile submarines, securing production into the late 2030s and supporting the AUKUS submarine transfer commitment.

items.title: Borr Drilling's Prospector 5 lands four-well letter of award from BW Energy, Gabon
items.summary: Borr Drilling received a binding letter of award from BW Energy in Gabon for its Prospector 5 jackup rig, covering a firm four-well campaign of at least 320 days with options to extend by up to 220 days, expected to start Q3 2026 in West Africa.

sections.title: Regulatory & Compliance Changes
sections.description: Rule changes from IMO, EU, classification societies and export-control authorities affecting marine, offshore and defence operators.

items.title: IMO PFOS firefighting foam ban enters into force 1 January 2026
items.summary: New SOLAS Chapter II-2 and HSC Code amendments prohibit fire-extinguishing media containing PFOS (a persistent 'forever chemical') above 10 mg/kg. New vessels with keels laid from 1 January 2026 must deliver PFOS-free; existing ships must remove and replace legacy foam stocks by their first survey on or after that date, requiring manufacturer PFOS-free declarations and documented disposal.

items.title: EU ETS reaches 100% emissions coverage for shipping from 1 January 2026
items.summary: The EU Emissions Trading System for maritime transport moved to full implementation on 1 January 2026, requiring shipowners to surrender allowances for 100% of verified CO2 emissions (up from 70% in 2025), and for the first time brings methane and nitrous oxide into scope — sharply increasing compliance costs, especially for LNG-fuelled vessels.

items.title: EU's 21st Russia sanctions package adds 41 more vessels to shadow fleet list
items.summary: The EU designated 41 additional tankers under its 21st sanctions package, pushing the total sanctioned 'shadow fleet' vessel list to nearly 600 ships, and expanded listing criteria to also capture vessels providing bunkering and support services to sanctioned tankers, triggering EU port-access bans and maritime service restrictions.

items.title: DNV publishes July 2026 class rules with new energy-transition notations
items.summary: DNV's July 2026 rule edition (in force 1 January 2027, early adoption by mutual consent) introduces notations including 'Shore power ready', 'Battery ready', and 'ER(ULEV)' for ultra-low-emission vessels, alongside relaxed corrosion-margin/structural requirements and streamlined fire-safety documentation for windfarm service vessels.

items.title: US State Department finalizes AUKUS ITAR exemption for defense trade
items.summary: DDTC published a final rule (effective early January 2026) adding ITAR section 126.7(c), exempting certain reexports, retransfers and temporary imports of defense articles among Australia, the UK and the US when properly authorized, and expanding 'Authorized User' status to UK/Australian government departments — easing licence-free defence trade among AUKUS partners.

items.title: IMO reconvenes Net-Zero Framework vote after October 2025 adjournment
items.summary: The IMO's Marine Environment Protection Committee adjourned its extraordinary session on the draft MARPOL Annex VI Net-Zero Framework (a global fuel standard and GHG pricing mechanism for ships above 5,000 GT) in October 2025, pushing final adoption to a reconvened session roughly 12 months later amid opposition led by the US — leaving shipowners in continued regulatory limbo on carbon levy design.

sections.title: Competitor Moves
sections.description: M&A, contract wins, product launches and strategic shifts among offshore contractors and modular/accommodation equipment providers.

items.title: Saipem-Subsea7 merger hit with EU Phase II antitrust investigation
items.summary: The European Commission opened an in-depth Phase II probe into the proposed Saipem/Subsea7 merger (to form 'Saipem7') over concerns it could reduce competition in offshore engineering and subsea umbilicals, risers and flowlines (SURF) services; Australian regulators are also conducting an in-depth review.

items.title: McDermott wins mega offshore EPCI contract from ADNOC for Umm Shaif
items.summary: McDermott, with its Qingdao McDermott Wuchuan (QMW) joint venture, was awarded a mega (over $1 billion) EPCI contract by ADNOC for Package 4 of the Umm Shaif Integrated Gas Cap and Surface Pressure Boosting Project, covering a jacket and topside that will rank among the heaviest offshore modules ever installed in the Middle East.

items.title: Centurion Group expands Canadian rental footprint via Equipment World deal
items.summary: Centurion Group, parent of offshore accommodation module specialist H2M, acquired Equipment World Inc., an Ontario-based equipment sales, rental and maintenance provider, broadening Centurion's diversified multi-industry rental platform.

items.title: Wilhelmsen completes full exit from Edda Wind offshore wind vessel fleet
items.summary: Wilhelmsen sold its entire stake in Edda Wind's service operation vessel (SOV) and commissioning SOV fleet, including newbuilds under construction, to UK-based North Star and an affiliate of Navigare Capital Partners, ending its offshore wind vessel investment.

items.title: H2M launches redesigned lightweight offshore accommodation module
items.summary: H2M Offshore Accommodation (a Centurion Group company) launched a newly designed A60/DNV 2.7-1/ABS/USCG-certified ISO 20ft accommodation module aimed at offshore wind projects, manufactured with sister company Specialist Services and already deployed on a Taiwan offshore wind project.

items.title: Armoda delivers single-lift fiberglass modular living quarters for dredging barge
items.summary: Modular fabricator Armoda (New Iberia, Louisiana) completed and installed a custom 36'x32'x12' fiberglass modular living quarters unit as a single-lift structure on a dredging barge, housing a 12-person crew with staterooms, galley and laundry facilities.

sections.title: Regional Activity (UAE, KSA, South East Asia)
sections.description: Offshore, energy and defence developments across the UAE, Saudi Arabia and South East Asia.

items.title: Technip Energies wins ADNOC Offshore engineering contract via L&T
items.summary: Technip Energies was selected by Larsen & Toubro (L&T) for a significant detailed engineering services contract on a major ADNOC Offshore project in the UAE, covering new offshore facilities and modifications to existing infrastructure. The award follows L&T's lead role in a consortium that secured an EPCIC contract worth over $1.7bn from ADNOC Offshore.

items.title: Abu Dhabi Ship Building signs Dh1.3bn Leonardo deal for Kuwait missile boats
items.summary: Abu Dhabi Ship Building (ADSB), an EDGE Group subsidiary, signed a Dh1.3bn (~€320m) contract with Italy's Leonardo to equip Kuwait's new Falaj 3-configuration Al Dorra-class missile boats with combat systems, radar and guns. ADSB is building eight of the vessels for the Kuwaiti Navy under a broader export program.

items.title: AD Ports Group earmarks $667m for 2026 port infrastructure investment
items.summary: Abu Dhabi-listed AD Ports Group set 2026 capital expenditure of AED2.45bn ($667m) for port infrastructure development, following record 2025 revenue (AED20.77bn, up 20%) and profit. The plan includes expansion at Khalifa Port and further capex for LNG/LPG storage terminal development through 2028.

items.title: Saipem wins $500m Aramco offshore contract for Safaniya trunkline
items.summary: Saipem was awarded a contract release purchase order by Saudi Aramco worth ~$500 million for EPCI of a 48-inch, ~65km offshore/12km onshore trunkline and related subsea infrastructure at the Safaniya oil field, under its existing long-term agreement with Aramco.

items.title: Saipem awarded two more Saudi offshore contracts worth ~$400m
items.summary: Saipem secured two additional offshore contracts in Saudi Arabia (CRPOs under its long-term agreement with Aramco) worth a combined ~$400 million, covering further infrastructure work at the Safaniya oil field, building on its February 2026 award in the same field.

items.title: Petronas launches Malaysia Bid Round 2026 to boost E&P investment
items.summary: Petronas, via Malaysia Petroleum Management, launched Malaysia Bid Round 2026 (MBR 2026) on 11 February 2026, offering nine exploration blocks (including a frontier Sandakan Basin block) plus six ready-to-develop Discovered Resource Opportunities, as Malaysia seeks RM50-60bn in annual upstream investment.

items.title: Vietnam begins construction of first indigenous multipurpose frigate
items.summary: Vietnam started construction on 10 August 2026 of its first domestically designed multipurpose (anti-submarine warfare) frigate, roughly 2,500-3,000 tonnes, built by Da Nang-based Song Thu Corporation with a high proportion of indigenous weapons and sensor systems from Viettel, reducing reliance on Russian equipment.

items.title: HD Hyundai delivers first Rajah Sulayman-class OPV to Philippine Navy
items.summary: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries delivered the first of six 2,400-ton Rajah Sulayman-class offshore patrol vessels to the Philippine Navy in February 2026, five months ahead of schedule, under a ₱30bn ($573m) contract signed in 2022; the remaining five vessels are due for sequential delivery through 2028.
